note: Base input rates in USD per million tokens, as DATE-EFFECTIVE tiers. A flat rate is a time bomb: Sonnet 5's introductory price expires 2026-08-31, and a hard-coded 2.00 would understate every figure by a third from 2026-09-01. Rates are list price. Real engagements reconcile against the customer's effective rate from their invoice, which is usually not list.

claude-opus-4-1.note: Deprecated. Priced because a trace being analysed is history: a workload that ran on it last month still has to reconcile against last month's invoice.

claude-sonnet-4.note: Retired on the first-party API, still served on Bedrock and Google Cloud. Those are partner-priced surfaces; this rate is the Anthropic list price and applies to anthropic/direct only.

claude-haiku-3-5.note: Retired on the first-party API, still served on Bedrock and Google Cloud. Same caveat as claude-sonnet-4.

additions_2026_07_30.cross_check: Every one of the four cross-checks against the multipliers this registry already records. Haiku 3.5 is the tightest: 0.80 base, 1.00 write-5m is 1.25x, 1.60 write-1h is 2x, 0.08 read is 0.1x. A row that failed this check would mean either the rate or the multiplier is misread, and both feed the same dollar figure.
additions_2026_07_30.why: These four were named in providers.json with a cache minimum but carried no rate, so cost.price refused them and every request on them was excluded from spend, from the ratios and from invoice reconciliation. A client still on Sonnet 4 got a report about a subset of their traffic. Two are retired on the first-party API and priced anyway, because a trace is history: the workload already ran and its invoice already exists.

rate_scope.why: These rates are Anthropic FIRST-PARTY list prices. They are not a global price for Claude. Anthropic's own pricing page draws the line: the first-party rates also cover Microsoft Foundry, which bills through the Microsoft Marketplace at standard API rates, while Bedrock and Vertex are partner-operated and priced by the cloud provider that invoices you. Before this scope existed, cost.price took the rate from `models` for ANY target, so a Bedrock trace was silently priced at Anthropic rates and produced a confident dollar figure the client's AWS bill would not match. Wrong-surface pricing is worse than no pricing: no pricing abstains and says so, wrong pricing publishes.

amazon-bedrock/converse.why_no_rows: Not recorded because AWS does not appear to publish current-generation Claude-on-Bedrock rates in any machine-readable form. Three independent sources checked 2026-07-31. (1) The Price List API offer file for AmazonBedrock, 15,090,427 bytes and 10,995 products: exactly 10 rows mention Claude at all, covering five legacy models -- Claude 2.0, 2.1, 3 Haiku, 3 Sonnet and Instant -- with no 4.x or 5 family and no cache read/write SKUs. (2) The feed the AWS pricing page itself renders from (b0.p.awsstatic.com/pricing/2.0/meteredUnitMaps/bedrock/USD/current/bedrock.json, manifest date 2026-07-23, 2,090,249 bytes decompressed): zero occurrences of the string 'claude' -- it is rateCode-to-price only, and the names come from joining the SKU catalog above, which does not carry them. (3) Scraping the HTML pricing page returned two stale models and a note that was visibly bleed-through from another row. A rate reached by guessing parity with first-party is exactly the failure this scope exists to prevent, so there are no rows. Re-check before assuming this is still true.

google-cloud/vertex.why_no_rows: Not recorded. The Vertex AI generative-ai pricing page (checked 2026-07-31) has no Anthropic section at all -- it covers Google's own models, CodeMender and grounding. The #claude-models anchor that Anthropic's docs link to no longer resolves to a Claude table. Re-check before assuming this is still true.

unknown/unattributed.why_no_rows: Not a real surface. This is what an ingest uses when a row carries no provider metadata at all, so the surface was never stated and cannot be inferred. It used to default to anthropic/direct, which meant a proxy export fronting Bedrock or Vertex was priced at Anthropic first-party rates and published a reconciled-looking total no cloud bill would match -- the exact failure the rate scope exists to prevent, entering through the one door the scope could not see, because the surface it was checking had been fabricated from an absence. Pass --target-id to state the surface, or --effective-rate to price it from the bill.

rate_scope.how_to_price_these: Supply the rate from the customer's own cloud invoice via --effective-rate / effective_rate=. That is the better number regardless: partner rates vary by region and endpoint type, Anthropic documents a 10% premium on regional and multi-region endpoints over global ones for Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.5 and later, and enterprises at this volume rarely pay list anyway.

provenance.source_quote: The prices above are Anthropic first-party API rates - they also apply to Claude on Microsoft Foundry, which is billed through the Microsoft Marketplace at standard API rates. Claude on Amazon Bedrock and Vertex AI is partner-operated with separate pricing.
provenance.cross_check: The same page's model table independently corroborates that these are different surfaces: Sonnet 4 and Haiku 3.5 are marked 'retired, except on Bedrock and Google Cloud', so those surfaces already differ from first-party in which models they even serve.
